inputs.content:
# Palisade Docs: raise prices while churn is rising? — briefing pack

> **Synthetic benchmark data.** The company, people, competitors and every figure in this pack are fictional. They were generated for a reasoning benchmark and are internally consistent, but they are not real market data.

## 1. Context

Palisade Docs sells document-workflow and e-signature software. ARR is $86.0M from 7,400
customers in three segments. Monthly customer churn has risen over the past year, and the CFO wants a price increase.

**Decision maker:** CEO Ravi Menon, deciding on the 2027 pricing plan with the leadership team in December 2026.

## 2. Decision question

**Should Palisade raise prices in 2027 while customer churn is rising, and if so, how?**

## 3. Objectives and constraints

- Grow ARR at least 15% in 2027 (from $86.0M).
- Keep net revenue retention above 100% overall.
- Price changes apply at renewal; enterprise contracts follow their own terms.

## 4. Current views inside the company

- **CFO:** "Raise list prices 12% on every plan at renewal from January 2027. That is $10.3M of ARR. Churn is an
  onboarding problem, not a price problem."
- **CEO's concern:** "Churn is going up. A price rise now could push it higher."
- **Head of Customer Success:** "The 2025 promotion brought in customers who never set the product up."

## 5. Segments

**Table 1. Segments, mid-2026**

| Segment | Customers | ARR, $M | Monthly logo churn H1 2025 | Monthly logo churn H1 2026 | Net revenue retention (trailing 12 months) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SMB | 5,900 | 21.0 | 2.0% | 3.1% | 94% |
| Mid-market | 1,350 | 41.0 | 0.6% | 0.8% | 112% |
| Enterprise | 150 | 24.0 | 0.2% | 0.2% | 118% |

SMB = 1–50 employees, self-serve, monthly or annual plans. Mid-market = 51–1,000 employees, annual contracts.
Enterprise = over 1,000 employees, mostly multi-year contracts.

## 6. The 2025 SMB promotion

- From February to August 2025, new self-serve SMB customers got 50% off for their first six months. The
  promotion brought in 2,100 SMB customers who are still counted in the base above (about $4.4M of ARR at full price).
- Share of new customers who sent at least five documents in their first month: 41% for the promotion cohort,
  72% for other cohorts.
- Monthly churn in H1 2026 for SMB customers who did **not** come through the promotion: 2.1% (H1 2025 for the
  same kind of customers: 2.0%).

**Table 2. Main churn reason "price / found a cheaper option", share of churned customers who answered the exit survey**

| Group | Share citing price |
|---|---|
| all SMB churners H1 2025 | 19% |
| all SMB churners H1 2026 | 34% |
| promo-cohort churners H1 2026 | 52% |
| non-promo SMB churners H1 2026 | 18% |

Most promotion-cohort customers who left did so within two months of the discount ending.

## 7. Competitor

- **Inkwell** launched a Starter plan at $9 per user per month in October 2025. Palisade's SMB plan is $15 per
  user per month; Business plan $29; Inkwell Pro $24.
- Palisade's win rate in SMB deals where Inkwell was considered fell from 51% (H1 2025) to 38% (H1 2026).
  Inkwell has not been seen in mid-market or enterprise deals with more than 200 seats.

## 8. Pricing history and tests

- **2023 SMB price increase:** +8% at renewal. SMB monthly churn rose from 1.8% to 2.3% for six months, then
  settled at 1.9%.
- **2024 mid-market test:** +10% list price for new mid-market sign-ups for three months: conversion 23.1%
  against 23.6% for the control group (difference not statistically significant).
- **Enterprise:** 60% of enterprise ARR is under contracts that cap annual price increases at 7%. 40% of
  enterprise ARR renews in 2027, as does 85% of mid-market ARR and all SMB ARR.

## 9. Product and customer evidence

- Mid-market and enterprise customers rate Palisade's integrations and audit trail as the main reasons they stay
  (customer advisory board, 2026).
- SMB customers who send fewer than five documents in their first month churn at about three times the rate of
  those who send more.

## 10. Other material

- **Board dashboard (Q2 2026):** "Monthly churn: 1.4% → 2.3%." The dashboard does not define the measure.
- **Head of Customer Success:** "An onboarding programme will halve SMB churn within two quarters."

## 11. Uncertainties

- How price-sensitive non-promotion SMB customers are now that Inkwell exists.
- Whether the promotion cohort can be activated, or will mostly churn regardless.
- Whether the mid-market test (new sign-ups) predicts how existing customers react at renewal.

storyline.governing_thought: Raise 2027 prices where customers stay (mid-market 12%, enterprise at contract terms, established SMB 8%) and activate the promotion cohort instead

exec_summary.text: Churn is rising because of the 2025 promotion cohort, not because SMB customers have turned against our price

sub_points.text: Outside the promotion, SMB churn is 2.1%, against 2.0% a year earlier
41% of the cohort activated in month one, compared with 72% of others

exec_summary.text: The CFO's 12% on every plan would add $7.6M in 2027, not $10.3M, and hits SMB where Inkwell already wins

sub_points.text: Renewal timing and caps keep a quarter of the $10.3M out of 2027
Our SMB win rate against Inkwell fell from 51% to 38% in a year

exec_summary.text: A rise can work where customers stay: mid-market, enterprise and SMB customers outside the promotion

sub_points.text: The mid-market rise pays unless churn more than doubles, to 1.7%
8% for established SMB customers nets about $0.7M at 2023's reaction

exec_summary.text: This mix takes existing customers just past the 15% target; new business must cover a weaker year

sub_points.text: Five gates, all checked by mid-2027, let us scale the plan back

next_steps.action: Approve the 2027 price plan: mid-market +12%, enterprise at contract terms, SMB +8% outside the promotion cohort
Confirm how NRR is calculated and set one churn measure for the board dashboard
Launch an onboarding programme for the promotion cohort and track its monthly churn
Prepare mid-market and enterprise renewal talks around integrations and the audit trail
Set 2027 new-business targets to cover the stress-case gap and review gates each quarter

constraints.item: Price changes apply only at renewal; 85% of mid-market and 40% of enterprise ARR renew in 2027
constraints.effect: cuts the CFO's $10.3M to $7.6M reachable in 2027; every plan figure uses renewal shares

constraints.item: 60% of enterprise ARR is capped at 7% a year
constraints.effect: enterprise counted at 7% on capped and 12% on other renewing ARR
base case clears it by only $0.8M from existing customers; stress misses by $3.3M; titles say 'just clear' and the gap goes to new business

constraints.item: SMB NRR of 94% may include the promotion cohort's step-up from 50% off to full price (not defined in the pack)
constraints.effect: stress case removes up to $2.2M; first gate is to confirm the definition before approval

constraints.item: Cost of the onboarding programme is not in the pack
constraints.effect: activation value is shown before programme cost and kept out of the base case

alternatives.option: CFO plan: 12% on every plan at renewal
alternatives.why: only $0.6M more even on a generous 2023-style SMB reaction, and that extra rests on a 12% step for the promotion cohort, which leaves over price

alternatives.option: Mid-market and enterprise only, SMB list prices held
alternatives.why: safest for SMB but leaves only $0.1M of headroom on the target; established SMB customers show no new price sensitivity

alternatives.option: Raise all SMB except the promotion cohort by 12% rather than 8% (sceptic's proposal)
alternatives.why: adopted the exclusion of the promotion cohort; kept 8% because it is the only SMB rise with a measured reaction and 12% takes the plan to $16.80 against Inkwell's $9

failure_threshold.driver: mid-market monthly churn on renewed accounts
failure_threshold.threshold: above about 1.0% a month existing customers miss the 15% target; above about 1.7% the mid-market rise stops adding ARR
failure_threshold.range: 2027 growth from existing customers 11.2% stress / 16.0% base / 17.1% high

consistency.headline: Raise 2027 prices where customers stay and activate the promotion cohort instead of pricing it
consistency.fix: exec item 4 and slide 11 say 'just clear' the target and name new business as the buffer, instead of claiming the target is reached

gap.base_case: $99.7M from existing customers in the base; $95.6M in stress, $3.3M short

closers.option: New-customer ARR target sized to the stress gap
closers.size: about $3.3M in stress, nothing needed in base

cases.stress: $95.6M, +11.2%: mid-market churn up by half and SMB NRR without the promotion step-up; the price rises still add ARR and NRR stays at 111%

gates.threshold: counts the promotion step-up to full price, up to $2.2M

lead_message.text: Churn is rising almost only in SMB, where the monthly rate jumped by more than half in a year

slides.rationale: Two periods compared across three segments -> clustered columns, SMB highlighted
slides.unit_line: **Monthly logo churn**, % of customers, by segment, H1 2025 and H1 2026

sidebar.header: The churn problem sits where customers can leave at any time
sidebar.caption: relative rise in SMB monthly logo churn in a year
bullets: **SMB:** self-serve monthly and annual plans, and the only segment where Inkwell competes head-on
**Mid-market:** a small rise on annual contracts, still a quarter of the SMB rate
**Scale:** SMB is 80% of customers but 24% of ARR, so logo churn overstates the revenue at risk

footnotes: Logo churn = share of customers lost per month. The board dashboard's "1.4% → 2.3%" is undefined and matches no segment measure (backup); this deck uses segment logo churn throughout

lead_message.text: The 2025 promotion explains the SMB rise: customers outside it churn at 2.1%, almost the same as a year ago

slides.rationale: Same metric for four groups, promotion cohort singled out -> bar in logical order; the cohort value is our estimate, so a basis strip
slides.unit_line: **SMB monthly logo churn**, % of customers, by group

sidebar.header: One cohort drives most of the losses
sidebar.caption: of SMB customers lost each month came through the 2025 promotion
bullets: **Promotion cohort:** 36% of SMB customers, churning at 2.3 times the rate of the rest
**Timing:** most of the cohort's leavers went within two months of the 50% discount ending
**Everyone else:** no sign that price or product has worn out with established SMB customers

basis.header: How we derived the cohort's churn

terms.caption: implied monthly churn of the cohort

footnotes: Cohort churn is derived from the segment and non-promotion rates with mid-2026 customer counts as weights; the pack does not report it directly

lead_message.text: The promotion cohort cites price because it never adopted the product, activating at little more than half the usual rate

slides.rationale: One claim, two pieces of evidence (exit survey, activation) -> two panels, no arrow

panels.header: Price complaints rose only through the promotion cohort
panels.unit_line: **Churners naming price as main reason**, % of exit-survey respondents

panels.header: Fewer than half of the cohort set the product up in month one
panels.unit_line: **New customers sending 5+ documents in month one**, % of cohort

slides.so_what: Low first-month use triples churn, so activation, not price, is this cohort's lever
footnotes: Exit survey covers churned customers who answered it; "price" = main reason "price / found a cheaper option"

lead_message.text: Only about $7.6M of the CFO's $10.3M can land in 2027, because a quarter of it renews later or is capped

slides.unit_line: **ARR added by a 12% list price rise at renewal**, $ millions, 2027

sidebar.header: Contracts, not customers, cut the headline
sidebar.caption: of the CFO's $10.3M cannot land in 2027
bullets: **Enterprise:** the largest cut, since 60% of its ARR renews after 2027
**Mid-market:** 15% of its ARR renews after 2027 and takes the rise in 2028
**SMB:** renews in full in 2027, so it supplies 33% of what remains, all from the segment where churn is rising

footnotes: $86.0M × 12% = $10.3M, the CFO's figure. Assumes the 60% of enterprise ARR under 7% caps is spread evenly across renewal years
Before any churn response to the rise

lead_message.text: In SMB, a further rise would widen a price gap that is already costing us deals against Inkwell

slides.rationale: Two sides of one risk (price gap, lost deals) -> two panels, no arrow

panels.header: A 12% rise would put our SMB plan at nearly twice Inkwell Starter
panels.unit_line: **List price**, $ per user per month, 2026 and after a 12% rise

panels.header: Since Starter launched, we lose most SMB deals where Inkwell is in the running
panels.unit_line: **Palisade win rate in SMB deals where Inkwell was considered**, %

slides.so_what: The rise lands on the segment where Inkwell competes, on top of a cohort that left when its last price step came
footnotes: Inkwell launched Starter in October 2025; Palisade's SMB plan is $15 and Business $29 per user per month

lead_message.text: Larger customers can carry a rise: they retain 112% and 118% of revenue, and a price test barely moved sign-ups

slides.rationale: Three proof points for one claim -> KPI tiles with drivers
slides.unit_line: **Retention and price response, mid-market and enterprise**, trailing 12 months and 2024 test

items.caption: mid-market net revenue retention
drivers: Customers name integrations and the audit trail as their main reasons to stay
Inkwell has not been seen in deals above 200 seats; smaller mid-market deals are the exposed edge
85% of mid-market ARR renews in 2027, so most of a rise lands this year

items.caption: enterprise net revenue retention
drivers: Same integration and audit-trail reasons to stay
60% of enterprise ARR is capped at 7% a year
Only 40% renews in 2027; the rest takes a rise later

items.caption: change in mid-market conversion at +10% list price, not significant
drivers: 2024 test on new sign-ups: 23.1% converted, against 23.6% in the control group
Existing customers at renewal were not tested, so the first 2027 renewals are the real test

footnotes: Reasons to stay from the 2026 customer advisory board; net revenue retention as reported in the briefing pack (definition not given)

lead_message.text: As a result, the mid-market rise pays for itself unless monthly churn more than doubles, to about 1.7%

slides.rationale: Our breakeven estimate is the point of the slide -> equation with assumptions
slides.unit_line: **Mid-market monthly logo churn at which a 12% rise stops adding ARR**, % of customers, 2027

terms.caption: extra monthly churn the rise can absorb: $4.2M added ÷ ($39.0M renewing ARR at the new price × 12 months)

body.assumptions_header: The breakeven rests on four simplifications
assumptions: Lost ARR in the year ≈ extra monthly churn × 12 months × renewing ARR at the new price (simple, not compounded)
Customers who leave over price are of average size
Expansion from seats and upgrades stays at today's rate; only churn reacts to the rise
Mid-market monthly logo churn starts from its H1 2026 level of 0.8%

footnotes: Breakeven for the rise itself; the 15% growth target is lost much earlier, at about 1.0% a month (gates, last section)

lead_message.text: Outside the promotion cohort, an 8% SMB rise would still net about $0.7M if customers react as they did in 2023

slides.rationale: Our estimate with a known precedent -> equation with assumptions
slides.unit_line: **ARR from an 8% rise for SMB customers outside the 2025 promotion**, $ millions, 2027

terms.caption: added: 8% on $16.6M of SMB ARR outside the promotion, all renewing in 2027
lost at the 2023 reaction: churn +0.5 pp for six months, +0.1 pp after (3.6% of ARR)
kept; the rise loses money only if the reaction is 2.1 times 2023's

body.assumptions_header: Why 8%, and why only these customers
assumptions: 8% is the one SMB rise we have measured; 12% would put the plan at $16.80 against Inkwell's $9, and its reaction is unknown
Their churn (2.1% compared with 2.0%) and price complaints (18% compared with 19%) have not moved since 2025
The promotion cohort keeps its price: 52% of its leavers cite price, and most left within two months of the last price step
The extra churn is applied to all of their ARR at the new $16.20 price for twelve months

lead_message.text: The recommended mix keeps most of the CFO's upside while sparing the customers most likely to leave over price
highlights: Recommended: mid-market 12%, enterprise at terms, SMB 8% outside the promotion

slides.rationale: Three options on the same criteria -> comparison table; growth estimates with their basis in the sidebar
slides.unit_line: **2027 pricing options**, $ millions of ARR at 2027 renewals

bullets: **CFO's extra $0.6M:** rests on a 12% step for a cohort that left within two months of its last one

rows.label: CFO: 12% on every plan
rows.note: Most ARR, but bets SMB on an unmeasured reaction

rows.label: Recommended: mid-market 12%, enterprise at terms, SMB 8% outside the promotion
rows.note: Prices only customers whose reaction we know

footnotes: Growth = trailing NRR by segment plus price uplift, net of the SMB churn response, before new customers. CFO row: 2023 reaction scaled by 12 ÷ 8 on all SMB ARR, generous for the promotion cohort
Enterprise at 7% on capped and 12% on other ARR renewing in 2027 in every row

lead_message.text: Activating the promotion cohort is worth up to $1.0M of ARR and a third off SMB churn, not the half promised

slides.rationale: Sizing the activation lever and testing the Customer Success claim -> equation
slides.unit_line: **ARR kept in 2027 if the promotion cohort churned like other SMB customers**, $ millions, best case

terms.caption: ARR of the 2,100 promotion customers at full price
more of them still with us after 12 months at 2.1% monthly churn than at 4.9% (77.5% against 54.7%)
ARR kept in 2027 at best, before the programme's cost

body.assumptions_header: Halving SMB churn is out of reach
assumptions: Best case: the cohort churns like other SMB customers from January, cutting SMB churn from 3.1% to 2.1%, by 32%
Halving SMB churn to 1.55% would need the cohort to churn at 0.56% a month, a quarter of the rate of established SMB customers
The onboarding programme's cost is not in the briefing pack and is not netted out
Whether the cohort can be activated at all is one of the pack's open questions; the gates track it

lead_message.text: Existing customers would just clear the $98.9M target in 2027 if retention holds, leaving new business as the only buffer

slides.rationale: ARR today to 2027 ARR through retention and price -> waterfall; stress and target in the sidebar
slides.unit_line: **ARR from existing customers, recommended plan, base case**, $ millions, today to end of 2027

sidebar.header: Base clears the target by $0.8M; stress does not

rows.label: Stress: mid-market churn up by half; SMB NRR without the promotion step-up

bullets: **NRR:** 116% in the base and 111% in stress, above the 100% floor
**High:** $100.7M if the promotion cohort is fully activated
**Stress gap:** about $3.3M, for new business to cover

footnotes: SMB's 94% NRR may include the cohort's step from 50% off to full price; the pack does not define NRR, so stress removes up to $2.2M

lead_message.text: Five gates let leadership scale the plan back before any rise costs more than it earns

slides.rationale: Gates with metric, threshold, timing and response -> table
slides.unit_line: **Decision gates for the 2027 pricing plan**, thresholds from the analysis on earlier pages

cells.text: Plan on the stress case and size new-business targets to the gap
15% at risk: raise new-business and activation targets
Rise no longer pays: hold remaining renewals at 7%
Above the 2023 reaction: stop the 8% for remaining SMB renewals
Activation is not working: stop extra onboarding spend, keep the price flat

slides.so_what: Every gate is checked by mid-2027, early enough to change the second half of the year's renewals
footnotes: Thresholds: 1.0% uses up the base case's $0.8M headroom; 1.7% is the mid-market breakeven; 2.6% is today's 2.1% plus the 2023 rise of 0.5 pp; 3.5% is halfway from the cohort's 4.9% to 2.1%
